name: What should I check before replacing cabinets in an older kitchen with no remodeling records?

mainEntity.name: What should I check before replacing cabinets in an older kitchen with no remodeling records?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Older kitchens should be inspected for leaks, dated wiring, deteriorated flooring, uneven walls, and previous alterations before new cabinets are ordered. Replacing visible cabinets without addressing concealed conditions can leave the same problems behind them.

**Context:** The age of the home does not automatically determine the scope, but existing conditions often affect installation. In San Diego County, the applicable permitting process depends on the city or unincorporated jurisdiction and the work involved.

**Key factors:**
- Moisture below sinks and near appliances
- Wall and floor condition
- Electrical capacity and outlet locations
- Prior remodeling quality

**Practical guidance:** Request a field review and document areas that will be concealed after installation. Decide in advance how unexpected repairs will be priced and approved.

Elite Remodeling & Design can include condition review in a broader residential remodeling plan.
acceptedAnswer.description: Check for leaks, moisture damage, uneven floors, out-of-square walls, electrical limitations, and prior alterations before ordering. Since hidden conditions can change the scope, agree on an inspection and change-approval process before demolition.
